title: Students' Low-cost Access to High-speed Internet Outside of School
what_it_is: Students' Low-cost Access to High-speed Internet Outside of School

sections.label: Broadband access for low-income households
sections.summary: Almost all households with school-going children have broadband, and IMDA programmes give low-income households subsidised devices and connectivity.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Almost all households with school-going children have access to broadband.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA)'s NEU PC Plus and Home Access programmes provide a subsidised device and broadband connectivity to low-income households, including those with school-going children.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: From January 2020 to September 2021, over 20,000 low-income households with school-going children have benefited through the NEU PC Plus programme.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: During the recent full Home-Based Learning in May 2021, schools loaned out Internet-enabling devices to students who lacked Internet access at home.

sections.label: Broadband speed increase to 500Mbps
sections.summary: In 2020, broadband speed under IMDA's NEU PC Plus and Home Access programmes was increased from 300Mbps to 500Mbps.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Most recently, in 2020, broadband speed under IMDA’s NEU PC Plus and Home Access programmes were increased from 300Mbps to 500Mbps.

sections.label: Reapplication for Home Access beneficiaries
sections.summary: Home Access and NEU PC Plus beneficiaries can reapply after two years with no limit if they meet eligibility criteria.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: I appreciate his concern for those who may be in a bit more disadvantaged situation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: I would just like to highlight to the Member that for the Home Access beneficiaries, they can actually reapply at the end of the two-year period, as long as they meet the eligibility criteria and there is actually no limit to the number of times they can apply, as long as they can meet the eligibility requirements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: And this applies also to the NEU PC Plus programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: I understand his concerns and we are committed to equip all Singaporeans with the basic affordable digital access.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: So, we will continue to review the provisions to meet the needs, especially of those who are in a more disadvantaged situation, so that they have easy and affordable access to high-speed Internet outside school and in common places.
